value.body: An avionics technician works on an aircraft's electrical, radio, navigation and instrument systems. Employers include airlines, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) firms and helicopter operators. The work is fault-finding and component replacement in hangars and on the ramp, under the supervision of a licensed engineer until you hold a licence yourself.

items.label: Licence
items.note: Needs DGCA module exams and logged practical experience

items.label: Estimated new AME supply
items.note: All AME streams, not only avionics
items.source: Government reply in Parliament, citing DGCA-approved AME training institutes (as reported)

items.label: AME licences issued by DGCA (cumulative)
items.note: Older cumulative figure; all licence categories
items.source: Lok Sabha reply, Ministry of Civil Aviation (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete an approved AME course in the avionics (B2) stream, then join an airline or MRO as a trainee or technician. Clearing DGCA module exams and logging the required experience leads to a B2 licence and certifying responsibility.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Using test equipment such as multimeters

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift and night work is common.
Next roles: licensed B2 engineer, then type-endorsed and supervisory roles.
Without a licence, work must be signed off by a certifying engineer.
